Before becoming the ninth Secretary-General of the United Nations in 2017, this Portuguese Socialist led his country as prime minister from 1995 to 2002 — who is he?
António Guterres (born 30 April 1949) is a Portuguese and East Timorese politician and diplomat who, since 2017, has served as the ninth Secretary-General of the United Nations.

The unexpected victory of vastly outnumbered English troops over the French on 25 October 1415 during the Hundred Years' War boosted English morale and lasted until 1429. What historic battle was this?
Battle of Agincourt ((t)) was an English victory in the Hundred Years' War. The Battle of Agincourt ( AJ-in-kor(t); French: Azincourt [azɛ̃kuʁ]) was an English victory in the Hundred Years' War.
Recording six visions seen by a prophet exiled in Babylon between 593 and 571 BC, this prophetic text follows Isaiah and Jeremiah in the Christian Bible — which text?
Book of Ezekiel is the third of the Latter Prophets in the Tanakh (Hebrew Bible) and one of the major prophetic books in the Christian Bible, where it follows Isaiah and Jeremiah.

Charles G. Dawes (August 27, 1865 - April 23, 1951) was the 30th vice president of the United States from 1925 to 1929 under President Calvin Coolidge.
When a 1952 coup destroyed Cuba's emerging democracy, a young lawyer named Fidel Castro tried first through the courts—then took up arms. Which revolution overthrew Fulgencio Batista's dictatorship?
Cuban Revolution was the military and political movement that overthrew the dictatorship of Fulgencio Batista, who had ruled Cuba from 1952 to 1959.

Dmitry Utkin (11 June 1970 - 23 August 2023) was a Russian military officer and mercenary.

Erich Honecker (25 August 1912 - 29 May 1994) was a German communist politician who led the German Democratic Republic (East Germany) from 1971 until shortly before the fall of the Berlin Wall in November 1989.

Harold Shipman (14 January 1946 - 13 January 2004) was an English doctor in general practice and serial killer.

Home Army (abbreviated AK) was the dominant resistance movement in German-occupied Poland during World War II.
Nicknamed "Bougie," this former Knesset member and welfare minister followed his father into Israel's presidency in 2021 — who is he?
Isaac Herzog (born 22 September 1960) is an Israeli politician who has been serving since 2021 as the president of Israel.
The second son of one president and younger brother of another, this Republican politician served as Florida's governor from 1999 to 2007 before an unsuccessful 2016 presidential bid. Who is he?
Jeb Bush (born February 11, 1953) is an American politician and businessman who served as the 43rd governor of Florida from 1999 to 2007.
After ascending to Judah's throne at age eight, this king ordered major religious reforms once a long-lost scroll of the Law turned up during temple repairs — who is he?
Josiah or Yoshiyahu (Biblical Hebrew) was the 16th king of Judah (c. 640-609 BC).
Backed early on by the Viet Cong and Chinese Communists, this force grew in the forests of eastern Cambodia and later ruled the country as Democratic Kampuchea — which movement was it?
Khmer Rouge is the name that was popularly given to members of the Communist Party of Kampuchea (CPK), and by extension to Democratic Kampuchea, which ruled Cambodia between 1975 and 1979.
He joined the Communist youth league in 1923 and rose to run the Soviet Union for eighteen years, longer than anyone but Stalin — which leader?
Leonid Brezhnev (19 December 1906 - 10 November 1982) was a Soviet politician who served as General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union from 1964 until his death in 1982.

Mahua Moitra (Bengali; born 12 October 1974) is an Indian politician and former investment banker.
Dubbed the 'Father of the Steam Navy' for modernizing the fleet, this officer commanded ships in the War of 1812 before ending Japan's isolation — who was he?
Matthew C. Perry (April 10, 1794 - March 4, 1858) was a United States Navy officer who commanded ships in several wars, including the War of 1812 and the Mexican-American War.

After her three-time-president husband died in exile, this Panamanian widow took over both his coffee business and his political party — then in 1999 became the only woman ever to be elected president of Panama. Who is she?
Mireya Moscoso (born 1 July 1946) is a Panamanian politician who served as the President of Panama from 1999 to 2004.

Named crown prince in 2006 during his half-brother's reign, he finally ruled for just three years from 2020 until his death in 2023, grappling with internal political disputes. Which Kuwaiti leader is this?

Born in British Hong Kong, this Canadian politician became a Toronto school board trustee in 1985, later served as an NDP member of Parliament, and has been mayor of Toronto since 2023 — who is she?

This Pakistani military officer overthrew Nawaz Sharif's government in a 1999 coup and went on to serve as the country's tenth president — who is he?

This Pennsylvania state treasurer, convicted of accepting a bribe in a state tax-processing scandal, shocked the nation by taking his own life live on camera during a 1987 press conference — who was he?
R. Budd Dwyer (November 21, 1939 - January 22, 1987) was an American politician who served as the 70th treasurer of Pennsylvania from 1981 until his suicide in 1987.
A right-wing populist with a reputation as abrasive and aggressive, this former cost accountant served as New Zealand's prime minister from 1975 to 1984. Who was he?

Ted Cruz (born December 22, 1970) is an American politician and attorney serving as the junior United States senator from Texas since 2013.

This horned Alpine folklore figure accompanies Saint Nicholas each December, swatting badly behaved children with birch rods while good kids get small gifts — who is he?

Mitanni: Ancient Hurrian-speaking state in northern Syria and southeast Anatolia.

Taking office in December 1983, this Argentine lawyer and social democrat was the first democratically elected president after the country's military 'National Reorganization Process' — who was he?
Raúl Alfonsín: President of Argentina from 1983 to 1989.
Deposed in a 2017 coup after ruling Zimbabwe for 37 years as both prime minister and president, who was this revolutionary-turned-leader?
Robert Mugabe: Leader of Zimbabwe from 1980 to 2017.

On a single 1929 day in a Chicago garage, seven men were lined against a wall and gunned down — some of the killers disguised as police — in a brutal flashpoint of Prohibition-era gang warfare. What is this killing known as?

Saint Valentine's Day Massacre: 1929 gang shooting in Chicago. The Saint Valentine's Day Massacre was the murder of seven members and associates of Chicago's North Side Gang on Saint Valentine's Day 1929.

This wave of mass production, standardization, and rapid scientific discovery, sometimes dubbed the Technological era, is generally dated between 1870 and the outbreak of World War I in 1914. What period was this?

Founded by Aleister Crowley in the early 1900s, this occult philosophy centers on discovering one's 'True Will' and the maxim 'Do what thou wilt shall be the whole of the Law' — what is it?
Thelema: New religious movement founded by Aleister Crowley.

Tungsten (also called wolfram) is a chemical element; it has symbol W (from German: Wolfram) and atomic number 74.
In what year did Hamish Harding die?
Hamish Harding: George Hamish Livingston Harding (24 June 1964 – 18 June 2023) was a British businessman, pilot and adventurer based in the United Arab Emirates (UAE).
In what year was Pluto discovered?
Pluto (minor-planet number 134340) is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, a ring of bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
TypeScript: Anders Hejlsberg. TypeScript (TS) is a high-level programming language that adds static typing with optional type annotations to JavaScript.
Pethidine: Pfizer. Pethidine, also known as meperidine and sold under the brand name Demerol among others, is a fully synthetic opioid pain medication of the phenylpiperidine class.
Who is credited with discovering Archaeopteryx?
Archaeopteryx: Carl Friedrich Häberlein. Archaeopteryx (lit. 'ancient wing'), sometimes referred to by its German name, "Urvogel " (lit. 'Primeval Bird') is an extinct genus of bird-like dinosaurs.
Who is credited with discovering Oganesson?
Oganesson: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Oganesson is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Og and atomic number 118.
Who is credited with discovering Cimetidine?
Cimetidine: John Colin Emmett. Cimetidine, sold under the brand name Tagamet among others, is a histamine H2 receptor antagonist that inhibits stomach acid production.
Who is credited with discovering Iridium?
Iridium: Smithson Tennant. Iridium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ir and atomic number 77.
A broad-spectrum benzimidazole drug, this medicine clears intestinal parasites from pinworm to hookworm to tapeworm — which agent is it?
Albendazole is a broad-spectrum antihelmintic and antiprotozoal agent of the benzimidazole type.
A balloon-like bulge at a weakened patch of vessel wall, it can turn lethal in the brain's circle of Willis or the aorta if it bursts — what is this?
Aneurysm is an outward bulging, likened to a bubble or balloon, caused by a localized, abnormal, weak spot on a blood vessel wall.
Founder of a prominent Russian design studio and an avid, famously foul-mouthed blogger, this designer and entrepreneur is also a member of the Tolstoy family — name this designer?
Artemy Lebedev (born 13 February 1975) is a Russian designer, entrepreneur and Internet personality.
Built under license from the Swiss Pilatus PC-9, this turboprop trainer serves the US Air Force, Navy, and Marine Corps and flies in Canada under the designation CT-156 Harvard — which aircraft?
Beechcraft T-6 Texan II is a single-engined, turboprop aircraft currently built by Textron Aviation, formerly manufactured by Raytheon Aircraft Company, which sold to Textron in 2007.
Born as Hughes Helicopters' Model 77 to replace the AH-1 Cobra, this twin-turboshaft attack helicopter packs a 30 mm chain gun and Hellfire missiles in a tandem cockpit — what is it?
Boeing AH-64 Apache (-) is an American twin-turboshaft attack helicopter with a tailwheel-type landing gear and a tandem cockpit for a crew of two.

Synthesized by the liver in response to inflammation, this ring-shaped blood molecule binds to the surface of dead or dying cells to activate the immune system's complement cascade. What is it commonly called?
C-reactive protein (CRP) is an annular (ring-shaped) pentameric protein found in blood plasma, whose circulating concentration rises in response to inflammation.
Which metabolic process is the polar opposite of anabolism, breaking large molecules such as proteins and lipids down into monomers while releasing energy, some of it lost as heat?
Catabolism is the set of metabolic pathways that breaks down molecules into smaller units that are either oxidized to release energy or used in other anabolic reactions.
Linked to repeated head trauma, this worsening neurodegenerative disease turns up in boxers and footballers — and even in soccer players, largely from heading the ball. What is it?

Chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) is a neurodegenerative disease linked to repeated trauma to the head. The encephalopathy symptoms can include behavioral problems, mood problems, and problems with thinking.
This highly poisonous member of the carrot family can grow to nearly 8 feet tall, with hollow, maroon-spotted stems and a famously unpleasant odor — what plant is it?
Conium maculatum (British English) or poison hemlock (in North America), is a highly poisonous flowering plant and a nitrophile weed species in the carrot family Apiaceae.
Nearly every genus in this taxonomic family of armadillos is extinct, except for one genus that still includes eight living species today. Name the family?
Dasypodidae is a family of mostly extinct genera of armadillos.
What flying insect, of which about 3,000 species exist, is known for its large compound eyes, two pairs of transparent wings, and often iridescent, metallic body coloration?
Dragonfly is a flying insect belonging to the infraorder Anisoptera below the order Odonata.
This discipline systematically applies natural science and mathematics to design solutions like bridges, pacemakers, and spacecraft under real-world constraints. What field is it?
Engineering is the practice of systematically applying natural science and mathematics to design and improve systems, devices, or processes that solve problems under constraints.
Colloquially called 'squirting,' this phenomenon involves fluid from the Skene's gland and is physiologically distinct from coital incontinence — what is it?
Female ejaculation is characterized as an expulsion of fluid from the Skene's gland at the lower end of the urethra during or before an orgasm.
This American video game businessman dropped out of Harvard to join Microsoft, where he worked on early Windows and a Doom port, before co-founding Valve Corporation in 1996 — who is he?
Gabe Newell (born November 3, 1962), also known by his nickname GabeN, is an American video game developer and businessman.
Comprising about 50 species native to tropical regions worldwide, this genus produces roughly 80% of the world's natural fiber and doubles as an oilseed crop — which genus?
Gossypium is a genus of flowering plants in the tribe Gossypieae of the mallow family, Malvaceae, from which cotton is harvested.

One of the first plants ever spun into fiber some 50,000 years ago, which fast-growing Cannabis sativa cultivar is grown for rope, textiles, paper, biofuel and food rather than its psychoactive punch?
Hemp is a plant in the botanical class of Cannabis sativa cultivars grown specifically for industrial and consumable use.

This large insect order includes sawflies, wasps, bees, and ants, with more than 150,000 described species, many of whose females have an egg-laying organ often modified into a stinger — what is it called?
Hymenoptera is a large order of insects, comprising the sawflies, wasps, bees, and ants.
This mild oxidizing agent and Lewis acid, with the formula FeCl3, is commonly used to purify water and to etch metal surfaces — which compound is it?
Iron(III) chloride is an inorganic compound with the formula FeCl3. The anhydrous derivative is a Lewis acid, while all forms are mild oxidizing agents.
This Confederate veteran and pharmacist sold the rights to his 1886 beverage recipe to Asa Griggs Candler for about $2,300 shortly before he died — who is he?
John Stith Pemberton (July 8, 1831 - August 16, 1888) was an American pharmacist, chemist, and Confederate States Army officer who is best known as the inventor of Coca-Cola.
Originally a water-retrieving gun dog from Italy's Po Delta marshes, this breed later became prized for hunting truffles once its wetland habitat was drained — what breed is it?
Lagotto Romagnolo is an Italian breed of dog.
Named after a pioneer of sterile surgery, this genus of rod-shaped bacteria can multiply even at refrigerator temperatures and causes a rare but serious foodborne illness — what is it?
Listeria is a genus of bacteria that acts as an intracellular parasite in mammals.
Formed from two glucose units linked by an alpha(1→4) bond, which disaccharide, a reducing sugar unlike sucrose, is released when starch breaks down during malting?
Maltose (or), also known as maltobiose or malt sugar, is a disaccharide formed from two units of glucose joined with an (14) bond.
More than 80% of cases trace to asbestos exposure, and it grows from the thin lining covering the lungs and other organs — which cancer is it?
Mesothelioma is a type of cancer that develops from the thin layer of tissue that covers many of the internal organs (known as the mesothelium).
This genus of edible sac fungi has a honeycomb-like cap of ridges and pits, is prized in French and Catalan cooking, and turns toxic if eaten raw or undercooked. What fungus is this?
Morchella is a genus of edible sac fungi closely related to anatomically simpler cup fungi in the order Pezizales (division Ascomycota).

Encompassing three distinct genetic conditions marked by nervous-system tumors, one type brings café au lait skin spots and scoliosis while another causes early-onset hearing loss and cataracts — which condition?
Neurofibromatosis (NF) refers to a group of three distinct genetic conditions in which tumors grow in the nervous system.
Which applied-math discipline, born from pre-WWII military planning and overlapping heavily with industrial engineering, hunts for the maximum profit or minimum cost in real-world problems?

Operations research (British), often shortened to the initialism OR, is a branch of applied mathematics that deals with the development and application of analytical methods to improve management and decision-making.
This Scottish biologist-turned-town-planner coined the word 'conurbation' and his work contains one of the earliest versions of 'think globally, act locally.' Who was he?
Patrick Geddes (2 October 1854 - 17 April 1932) was a Scottish biologist, sociologist, Comtean positivist, geographer, philanthropist and pioneering town planner.
This genus of spiders in the family Ctenidae is found mainly in northern South America, with a single species ranging into Central America — name this genus?
Phoneutria is a genus of spiders in the family Ctenidae.

Native to most of the Northern Hemisphere, this genus of 25 to 30 deciduous tree species includes poplars, aspens, and cottonwoods, one of which was the first tree ever fully DNA-sequenced — which genus?
Populus is a genus of 25-30 species of deciduous flowering plants in the family Salicaceae, native to most of the Northern Hemisphere.
This yellow-white fluid forms at sites of infection and inflammation — when trapped in tissue it's called an abscess, and near the skin's surface a pimple — name the substance?
Pus is an exudate, typically white-yellow, yellow, or yellow-brown, formed at the site of inflammation during infections, regardless of cause.
Also known as vitamin B2, this nutrient builds two key coenzymes for energy metabolism and may, taken orally, cut down on migraine headaches in adults — what is it?
Riboflavin is a vitamin found in food and sold as a dietary supplement.
Having coded his first game in high school and studied computer science in Tokyo, this man went on to lead Nintendo by championing fun over raw horsepower — who is he?
Satoru Iwata (December 6, 1959 - July 11, 2015) was a Japanese businessman, video game programmer and producer.
Element number 14 is a tetravalent non-metal sometimes called a metalloid, prized for the transistors and integrated circuits it makes possible — which one is it?
Silicon is a chemical element; it has symbol Si and atomic number 14.
A self-taught Indian genius of infinite series and number theory, he initially struggled to interest established mathematicians because his methods were so unfamiliar — who was he?
Srinivasa Ramanujan (22 December 1887 - 26 April 1920) was an Indian mathematician who worked during the early 20th century.
Deriving its name from a French word for crushed oak bark used in hide-curing, this class of astringent plant compounds binds to and precipitates proteins and other organic molecules — what is it?
Tannin (or tannoids) are a class of astringent, polyphenolic biomolecules that bind to and precipitate proteins and various other organic compounds including amino acids and alkaloids.
This genus of about 30 tree and shrub species is native across the temperate Northern Hemisphere, with its greatest diversity found in Asia — what genus is it?
Tilia is a genus of about 30 species of trees or bushes, native throughout most of the temperate Northern Hemisphere.
What is the medical term for having dangerously high levels of urea in the blood, typically caused by kidney failure?

Uremia is the condition of having high levels of urea in the blood. It is the signs, symptoms and results from laboratory tests which result from inadequate excretory, regulatory, and endocrine function of the kidneys.
These big cetaceans — everything in the group except dolphins and porpoises — count the hippopotamus as their closest living relative on land. What are they?
Whale are a widely distributed and diverse group of fully aquatic placental marine mammals.
The only living member of its entire mammalian order, this nocturnal African burrower uses its long snout and powerful claws to dig ants and termites out of their mounds — what animal is it?
Aardvark: Burrowing mammal native to Africa.
While bacteria and some plants may be biologically immortal, this universal process in humans slows reaction time even as knowledge tends to grow — what is it called?
Ageing: Biological process of getting older.
This genus of over 650 succulent species includes a 'true' member long used in pharmaceutical products, native to Africa, Madagascar, and the Arabian Peninsula — which genus?
Aloe: Genus of succulent flowering plants.
Struck off the medical register for 'serious professional misconduct,' this former surgeon authored the fraudulent 1998 Lancet paper falsely tying the MMR vaccine to autism — who is he?

Latin for 'worm-shaped,' this finger-like, blind-ended tube branches off the cecum and, though long considered vestigial, may actually serve as a reservoir for beneficial gut bacteria. What structure is this?
Appendix (anatomy): Tube attached to the intestine.
This ocean giant, recorded at up to 680 kg, has vanished from the Black Sea but still roams the Mediterranean and both sides of another major ocean — which fish?
Atlantic bluefin tuna: Species of fish. The Atlantic bluefin tuna (Thunnus thynnus) is a species of tuna in the family Scombridae.

Members of the family Ursidae walk flat on plantigrade paws tipped with five claws that can't retract — and though most eat meat, the giant panda among them is mostly herbivorous. What animal is this?
Made by combining phenol and acetone, this compound forms 65 to 70 percent of the world's polycarbonate plastics production — which chemical?
Bisphenol A: Chemical used in plastics, xenoestrogen.
Formerly called the Russian Wolfhound until 1936, this Russian sighthound breed was originally used for hunting wolves. What breed is it?
Named after the Greek word for butter via butyric acid, this colorless, highly flammable gas exists as two isomers and vaporizes quickly at room temperature — what alkane is it?
Native to Africa, the Middle East, and arid parts of Asia, this nocturnal, secretive wild cat is built for the chase with long legs and dramatically long tufted ears — which animal?
Also called bachelor's button, this European annual once grew as a common weed among grain fields but is now endangered there due to herbicides — what flower is it?
Centaurea cyanus: Species of flowering plant.
A sweet-smelling, colorless solvent now made as a precursor to refrigerants and Teflon, this organochloride once served as an inhaled anesthetic from the 19th century onward — what is it?
Chloroform: CHCl3, historical anaesthetic and common solvent.
Many species of this venomous snake can rear up and flare a hood when threatened — what is it?
Cobra: Index of animals with the same common name.
This common bowel condition produces hard, infrequent stools and can lead to hemorrhoids or fecal impaction, with hypothyroidism and diabetes among its underlying causes. What is it?
Constipation: Infrequent or difficult bowel movements.

First described by Linnaeus in 1767, this citrus-family plant native to the Indian subcontinent has aromatic leaves essential to South Asian cooking, especially in India and Sri Lanka — which species?

Curry tree: Species of flowering plant. It is native to the Indian subcontinent, southern China and mainland Southeast Asia, and it has been introduced to other parts of southeast Asia and to Australia.
Spread by mosquitoes in tropical regions, this virus is often mild but can turn severe with bleeding, plummeting platelet counts, and dangerously low blood pressure — what is it?
Synthesized from L-DOPA in the brain and kidneys, this catecholamine acts as a neurotransmitter and drives a major brain pathway tied to reward and motivation — what is it?
Dopamine: Organic chemical that functions both as a hormone and a neurotransmitter.
Element 99 was first discovered in the radioactive debris of the very first hydrogen bomb explosion in 1952 — what synthetic actinide is it?
Einsteinium: Chemical element with atomic number 99 (Es)
Named from the Latin word for hedgehog, this mammal family unites spiny Eurasian and African hedgehogs with their Southeast Asian cousins, the moonrats — which family?
Erinaceidae: Family of mammals. Erinaceidae (from Latin erinaceus, "hedgehog") is a family in the order Eulipotyphla, consisting of the hedgehogs and moonrats.

Nicknamed the 'yaffle' for its loud call, this bird has a bright red crown and a black moustache stripe, and feeds mostly on ants on the ground rather than drumming on trees like its relatives — what is it?

European green woodpecker: Species of bird. It is resident across much of Europe and the western Palearctic but in Spain and Portugal it is replaced by the similar Iberian green woodpecker (Picus sharpei).
Native to the Mediterranean and grown since ancient times, this teardrop-shaped fruit is technically a syconium and comes from the type species of a genus with over 800 members — what fruit is it?
Fig: Species of flowering plant, or its fruit.
Also called the Baader-Meinhof phenomenon or Red Car Theory, this cognitive bias makes you notice something everywhere right after you first learn about it — what is it?
Frequency illusion: Kind of cognitive bias. The name "Baader–Meinhof phenomenon" was coined in 1994 by Terry Mullen in a letter to the St.

A trained civil engineer who oversaw concerts at the Crystal Palace, this Englishman's program notes grew into a famous music dictionary — and he once hunted Vienna for lost Schubert manuscripts with Arthur Sullivan. Who was he?
George Grove: English engineer and writer on music (1820–1900)
Credited alongside Isaac Newton with inventing calculus, this German polymath also pioneered binary arithmetic and earned the nickname 'the last universal genius' — who is he?
This protein filament that grows from follicles in the skin is one of the defining traits of mammals, and its removal or styling carries different meanings across cultures — what is it?
Hair: Protein filament that grows from follicles found in the dermis, or skin.
This field of study focuses on the methodological principles of interpreting texts — especially biblical and philosophical writings — and is closely related to exegesis. What is it called?
Hermeneutics: The study of the methodological principles of interpretation. As necessary, hermeneutics may include the art of understanding and communication.
In Greek myth, this fragrant spring bulb sprang from the blood of a youth slain by a jealous west wind god who coveted his bond with Apollo — what flower is it?
Powered by four underperforming Lyulka turbojets, this aircraft became the first Soviet jet bomber to fly before being cancelled in September 1947 — which plane?
Ilyushin Il-22: 1947 Soviet bomber aircraft prototype. The Ilyushin Il-22, USAF/DOD designation Type 10, was the first Soviet jet-engined bomber to fly.
An Indian polymath and pioneer of radio microwave optics, he's also considered the father of Bengali science fiction — and even has a crater on the Moon named for him. Who was he?
Jagadish Chandra Bose: Physicist, biologist and botanist (1857–1937)
He wrote the first commercial anti-virus software in 1987, then later urged people to uninstall the product bearing his name and twice ran for U.S. president — who was he?
John McAfee: British and American programmer and businessman (1945–2021)
Nicknamed the 'honey bear' though unrelated to actual bears, this nocturnal rainforest mammal is the only member of its genus and a cousin of raccoons and coatis — which arboreal creature?
A hybrid of the citron and the bitter orange, this small evergreen tree may have first appeared in northeastern India, and its fruit's juice is about 5–6% citric acid — what is it?
Also called pseudocoma, this condition leaves a fully conscious patient paralyzed except for blinking and vertical eye movement, coined by two neurologists in 1966 — what is it called?
Locked-in syndrome: Condition in which a patient is aware but completely paralysed.
Nicknamed for a Native American tribe, this mulberry-family tree produces a bumpy, orange-like fruit that oozes sticky white latex and is rarely eaten by animals — what's its scientific name?
Maclura pomifera: Plant species in the fig family.
In 2014 this Stanford mathematician became the first woman and first Iranian to win the Fields Medal, honored for her work on the geometry of Riemann surfaces — who was she?
Aristotle called it the 'first philosophy' — the branch that probes existence itself, what all things have in common, and how reality is divided into categories of being. Which field is it?
This Israeli-American physician turned billionaire donor owns the Las Vegas Review-Journal and Dallas Mavericks, and was one of Donald Trump's largest financial backers — who is she?

Miriam Adelson: Israeli-American physician, billionaire, and conservative donor. Miriam Adelson (née Farbstein; born October 10, 1945) is an Israeli-American physician, businesswoman, philanthropist, and conservative political donor.
This Austrian-School economist founded anarcho-capitalism and called the state "the organization of robbery systematized and writ large" — which libertarian theoretician?
The sole species in its genus and a fixture of Mediterranean gardens, this drought-and-flood-tolerant shrub of the dogbane family is also called rose laurel or rosebay — what is it?
Nerium: Species of plant. It is the only species currently classified in the genus Nerium, belonging to subfamily Apocynoideae of the dogbane family Apocynaceae.
Practitioners of this field are sometimes mistaken for mere coin collectors, but they study all means of paying debts — even the horses the Kyrgyz once used as currency. What's the field called?
Numismatics: Study of currencies, coins and paper money.
Named from Greek words meaning 'porous bones,' this disorder causes bone density loss serious enough that fractures can occur with minor stress, especially in the elderly — what is it?
Osteoporosis: Skeletal disorder. Osteoporosis is the most common reason for a broken bone among the elderly.
This American physician-turned-clown founded the Gesundheit Institute in 1989 and travels the world dressing up to bring humor to hospital patients — who is he?
Named from the Greek word for 'apparition' due to their leaf-like camouflage, this insect order includes stick insects and leaf insects. What's it called?
Phasmatodea: Order of stick and leaf insects.
Members of this eukaryotic kingdom mostly make their own food with chlorophyll, though parasitic kinds have ditched photosynthesis entirely to feed off others — what kingdom is it?
Plant: Kingdom of organisms. Historically, as in Aristotle's biology, the plant kingdom encompassed all living things that were not animals, and included algae and fungi.
This corticosteroid treats conditions from rheumatoid arthritis to asthma but can cause bone loss and psychiatric side effects with long-term use — what is it called?
Prednisolone: Corticosteroid medication. It can be taken by mouth, injected into a vein, used topically as a skin cream, or as eye drops.
Often starting as a blood clot in the leg that travels to the lungs, this blockage can cause chest pain on breathing in, coughing up blood, and sudden death — what is the condition?

Pulmonary embolism: Blockage of an artery in the lungs. Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a blockage of an artery in the lungs by a substance that has moved from elsewhere in the body through the bloodstream (embolism).

Native to the eastern Himalayas and southwestern China, this small mammal sports dense reddish-brown fur, a ringed tail, and curved semi-retractile claws for climbing — and was the original bearer of its famous name. What is it?
Red panda: Species of mammal in Asia.
First created in 1994 near Darmstadt, Germany, this extremely radioactive synthetic element is named for the physicist who discovered X-rays — which element is it?
Roentgenium: Chemical element with atomic number 111 (Rg)
This Taiwanese-American physicist shared the 1976 Nobel Prize with Burton Richter for discovering the subatomic J/ψ particle. Who is he?
Samuel C. C. Ting: Nobel prize winning physicist.
Coined by Horace Walpole in 1754, this term for a lucky accidental discovery describes how penicillin, Post-it Notes, and the microwave oven all came about — what is it?

Thanks to extra joints in its skull, this legless, scale-covered reptile can swallow prey far bigger than its own head — and its paired organs sit one behind the other to fit a narrow body. What creature is it?
This rodent family includes tree-dwelling, ground-dwelling, and gliding members like chipmunks and prairie dogs, and traces its fossil record back to the Eocene epoch — which animal family?
Squirrel: Family of rodents. The squirrel family includes tree squirrels, ground squirrels (including chipmunks and prairie dogs, among others), and flying squirrels.
Designed by R. J. Mitchell with a distinctive elliptical wing and sunken rivets for minimal drag, this was the only British fighter kept in continuous production throughout World War II — what is it?
Supermarine Spitfire: British single-seat WWII fighter aircraft.
Known as the barn funnel weaver in North America and simply the house spider in Europe, this species belongs to the funnel-web family Agelenidae — which arachnid?
Shaped like a butterfly and sitting in the neck just below the Adam's apple, this endocrine gland secretes hormones that regulate metabolic rate — which gland is it?
Thyroid: Endocrine gland in the neck. The lower two thirds of the lobes are connected by a thin band of tissue called the isthmus (pl.: isthmi).
This ester of glycerol and three fatty acids is the main constituent of body fat and a major component of human skin oils — what is it?
Triglyceride: Any ester of glycerol having all three hydroxyl groups esterified with fatty acids.
Before becoming the first woman in space aboard a solo 1963 flight that orbited Earth 48 times, this cosmonaut worked in a textile factory and skydove as a hobby — who is she?
Valentina Tereshkova: Russian cosmonaut and politician (born 1937)
Denoted by the Greek letter lambda, this measure of a repeating wave's spatial period shrinks as frequency rises for a wave moving at constant speed — what is it called?
Wavelength: Distance over which a wave's shape repeats.
Native to South America and first cultivated by the Guaraní people, the steeped leaves of this holly-genus plant produce a caffeinated beverage — what is it?
Yerba mate: South American holly plant. Yerba mate or yerba maté ( YUR-bə MAH-tay), Ilex paraguariensis, is a plant species of the holly genus native to South America.
The symbol for tungsten is W. Tungsten is a chemical element; it has symbol W and atomic number 74.
The symbol for platinum is Pt. Platinum is a chemical element; it has symbol Pt and atomic number 78.

In what year was Alien first released?
Alien is a 1979 science fiction horror film directed by Ridley Scott and written by Dan O'Bannon, based on a story by O'Bannon and Ronald Shusett.

Godzilla Minus One: It is the 37th film in the Godzilla franchise, the 33rd film thereof produced by Toho, and the fifth installment in the Reiwa era.

Thor: The Dark World: 2013. It is the sequel to Thor (2011) and the eighth film in the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU).

Gayniggers from Outer Space is a 1992 English-language Danish satirical science fiction short film, directed by Danish performance artist Morten Lindberg.

X-Men: Apocalypse: 2016. X-Men: Apocalypse is a 2016 American superhero film based on the Marvel Comics superhero team the X-Men.
